name: Pu Luong
provinceNote: From 1 July 2025, Resolution 1686 created xã Pù Luông from old Thành Sơn, Lũng Niêm, and Thành Lâm. That commune is only part of the valley. Bản Hiêu and Son, Bá, and Mười sit in xã Cổ Lũng.
dotReason: Worth a special trip for the limestone rice valley
summary: Terraced rice, stilt-house nights, and trekking in Thanh Hoa. Sleep in a Thai or Muong house, walk the slopes when the crop is green or gold, and eat Cổ Lũng duck at the table. One night is the stay when this valley morning is the trip.
getThere: Hanoi by road, about 160 km or about 210 km.
seoTitle: Pu Luong travel guide — terraced rice, stilt-house nights, trekking
seoDescription: Rice terraces and a stilt house in Thanh Hoa, about 160 km or about 210 km from Hanoi, green in late May to early June and gold in September and October.
intro: You wake to terraced rice after a night in a stilt house, with the trek still ahead in the Pù Luông reserve. This is Pù Luông Nature Reserve, the valley in Thanh Hoa. The morning is the crop on the slopes and the posts under the house.

Stay if that valley at breakfast is the trip. Go to Mai Chau if Bản Lác is the trip. Bản Lác is in Mai Chau. Go to Ninh Binh if the boats are the trip. From 1 July 2025, Resolution 1686 made xã Pù Luông out of old Thành Sơn, Lũng Niêm, and Thành Lâm. That commune is only part of the valley. Bản Hiêu and the hamlets Son, Bá, and Mười sit in xã Cổ Lũng.

The conservation pages put the reserve about 210 km from Hanoi and list 17,662 hectares, of which 13,320 hectares are strict protection and 4,343 hectares are restoration. Those two zones add to 17,663. Vietnam Tourism lists about 160 km southwest, and a limousine of about 4.5 hours from Giáp Bát or Mỹ Đình. The 2021 decision lists 16,986.16 hectares. No minute count sits beside either kilometer. A car or a motorbike hired in Hanoi is the usual road. The mistake is booking the neighbor when the photograph you wanted is this valley in the morning.
gettingAround: Bicycles are what Vietnam Tourism says visitors are offered, on the valley road, with steeper lanes if you want them. Homestays often lend them without a charge. A local motorbike is occasional, not the usual hire. No commune bus was named. Many hamlets want cash, on one commercial guide.

The 2021 scheme puts the management board in thị trấn Cành Nàng, now inside xã Bá Thước, and it plans a visitor center there and at khu phố Vận Tải. Thác Hiêu is about 25 km from Cành Nàng on the provincial culture page. That kilometer has no second source. The waterfall is in old Cổ Lũng, now xã Cổ Lũng. One account describes five small falls and blue-green water. Another describes a stream of about 800 metres that splits into two branches and meets again above a pool. A walk of 6–8 km and 2–4 hours from Bản Đôn is one commercial guide.

The summit walk is a separate two-day trek inside special-use forest, from bản Pù Luông to bản Báng, about 11 km, with nearly 2 km steeper than 35 degrees, in a limited group. VietNamNet lists the height as 1,700 m and, in another sentence, as higher than 1,700 m. Vietnam Tourism lists 1,700 m. The conservation page says the Thai name means the highest peak. The airline guide says it means “núi lớn”. Newcomers are told to walk with a group or a local guide. Walk the summit only in that limited group. The species lists are the reserve inventory. They do not schedule an animal on the path.

A provincial article dated 19 Oct 2026 describes the Vietnam Jungle Marathon through forest, hamlets, terraces, and bamboo bridges, with the start and finish at Làng Leo. The distances are 70 km, 50 km, 25 km, and 10 km. The 70 km start is 04:00. The article date is not the gun time.

stayAreas.name: The valley
stayAreas.summary: Stilt-house homestays at Bản Đôn, old Thành Lâm, now inside xã Pù Luông, or around Bản Hiêu in xã Cổ Lũng. Terraces at the foot of the hill, and a campfire, rượu cần, xòe, and khắp in the evening at Bản Đôn.

eat: The meal is in the stilt house: Cổ Lũng duck, cơm lam, hill chicken, and rượu cần. Phố Đoàn is a roadside market on Thursday and Sunday.

Vietnam Airlines calls Cổ Lũng duck fragrant and low in fat, boiled, grilled, or xáo. Xáo is not defined there. Hải Vân, on 16 May 2022, dips the boiled bird in chẩm chéo made from rang mắc khén, fresh chili, ginger, salt, and herbs. The Bản Đôn list says vịt cỏ and does not say it is the same bird. Măng rừng is the house shoot, măng khô is the market shoot, and măng đắng is the Vietnam Airlines shoot, eaten with a dip or fried with forest pork. The three names are not one recipe. Hill chicken is firm, with crisp skin, grilled with lá mắc mật, on Vietnam Airlines. VietNamNet’s 16 Nov 2025 summit supper names grilled chicken, xôi đồ, rượu ngô, and rượu chuối. That camp rice is not xôi tím. Bản Đôn lists xôi tím and does not say where the color comes from.

Vietnam Airlines grills small stream fish with forest leaves, and cooks cơm lam in a bamboo tube. Rock snail is ốc đá at Bản Đôn. The 16 May 2022 market article also says ốc suối and ốc núi. Vietnam Airlines calls it a rainy-season snail, steamed with lemongrass or fried with lime leaf. Bản Đôn does not give a season. Lợn rừng is the Bản Đôn name and lợn cỏ is the Vietnam Airlines name. They are not one breed. VnExpress, 3 Jul 2023, describes thịt gác bếp for Thai households in Quan Hóa and Bá Thước. A 26 Sep 2026 market article also names thịt treo gác bếp among highland goods, including Phố Đoàn, with no cut and no smoke time.
interestsBody: The terraces are the reason to sleep here. Late May to early June is the green crop on the conservation pages and on Vietnam Tourism. September and October are the gold crop on those pages. A provincial trekking note calls both windows golden.
The houses are on stilts, in Thai and Muong hamlets. Bản Đôn is the usual base. The evening is a campfire on the hamlet floor, not a bar street.
Thác Hiêu, the two-day summit, and the Thursday and Sunday market at Phố Đoàn are the other outings.

interestGroups.title: Terraces on two calendars
interestGroups.summary: For the rice on the slopes, green in one window and gold in the other.
body: Late May to early June is the green young rice on the conservation pages and on Vietnam Tourism. September and October are the ripe gold crop on those same pages. A provincial trekking note calls both May–June and September–October ripe and golden. Bản Đôn is busiest in February, March, September, and October. Morning is the hour for mist on the hills.
Bamboo water wheels lift stream water onto the fields. Vietnam Tourism calls them a Thai marker. They are scattered. No single wheel has an address on that page.

A provincial trekking note separates a harder Son–Bá–Mười line and a Làng Bầm forest path from an easier walk, Bản Đôn to bản Ngòn and bản Leo, for people who want the hamlets more than the summit. It tells newcomers to take a guide. No guide fee was listed. Son, Bá, and Mười are three hamlets in old Lũng Cao, now xã Cổ Lũng.

blocks.heading: Two rice windows
paragraphs: Late May to early June is green young rice. September and October are ripe gold. Those are the conservation pages and Vietnam Tourism. A provincial trekking note calls both windows ripe and golden.

blocks.heading: The easier walk
paragraphs: The easier line is Bản Đôn to bản Ngòn and bản Leo. Son–Bá–Mười and the Làng Bầm forest path are the harder lines. Newcomers are told to take a guide.

cards.title: Valley terraces
cards.summary: Come for the crop on the limestone slopes. Late May to early June is green. September and October are gold. One trekking note calls both windows golden.

interestGroups.title: Stilt houses of the Thai and Muong
interestGroups.summary: For a night in a house on posts, with the fire on the hamlet floor.
body: Vietnam Tourism says the reserve is home to Thai and Muong people and that the houses are on stilts. Bản Đôn, in old Thành Lâm and now inside xã Pù Luông, is mostly Thai. The evening there is a campfire, rượu cần, xòe Thái, and khắp. Xòe is also held for guests on ordinary nights, not only on a festival date. A feature lists a UNESCO date of 15 Dec 2021 for xòe Thái. Check that date on arrival. The night here is the hamlet circle.

Old Thành Lâm is where a political-school page names lễ hội Căm Mương, lễ hội cơm mới, and a culture day, without dates. A 2022 culture day is what the xòe feature describes. The evening is the hamlet floor.

cards.title: A house on posts
cards.summary: Sleep in a Thai or Muong stilt house. Bản Đôn is the usual base, with the fire after dark.

faqs.q: How far is Pu Luong from Hanoi?
faqs.a: The conservation pages list about 210 km. Vietnam Tourism lists about 160 km southwest, and a limousine of about 4.5 hours from Giáp Bát or Mỹ Đình. No minute count sits beside either kilometer.

Decision 495 of 27 Mar 1999: 17,660 hectares. The conservation pages: 17,662 hectares, with 13,320 strict and 4,343 restoration. Decision 3001 of 8 Nov 2001: 16,982.6 hectares. Decision 2463 of 16 Jul 2013: 17,171.03 hectares. Decision 1976 of 30 Oct 2014: 17,171.53 hectares. Decision 3392 of 31 Aug 2021: 16,986.16 hectares, with an appendix strict-protection subtotal of 10,953.27 hectares. The management page also lists strict 12,561.60, restoration 4,300.4, service 216.03, and other land 93.0, which add to the 2013 total rather than to 16,986.16. Vietnam Tourism says more than 17,600 hectares.

faqs.q: When is the rice, and when are the festivals?
faqs.a: Late May to early June is the green crop, and September and October are the gold crop, on the conservation pages and on Vietnam Tourism. A trekking note calls both windows golden. Lễ hội Căm Mương, the new-rice rite, and the valley culture day have no 2026 date in the sources.

season.label: Green late May, gold in September
season.note: Late May to early June is green young rice on the conservation pages and on Vietnam Tourism. September and October are ripe gold on those pages. A provincial trekking note calls both windows ripe and golden, cool, and with little rain. Bản Đôn is busiest in February, March, September, and October. Vietnam Tourism also says the valley is visitable in any month, and that summer stays cooler than the lowland because of limestone, forest, and few people. The airline guide says avoid July and August as storm months, with slippery roads. The conservation pages and Vietnam Tourism do not say that.
